title: i18n frameworks
description: i18n frameworks externalize every user-visible string: keys in code, translations in locale files, the framework resolving at runtime. The architecture is t('key', params) everywhere — no hardcoded strings. Frameworks (react-intl, i18next, gettext) add pluralization, formatting, and locale negotiation. The rule is absolute: a hardcoded string is a bug.
mechanism: t(key, vars) lookups; locale files (JSON/PO); fallback chain (es-MX -> es -> en); locale negotiation from the OS/browser. Lint bans hardcoded UI strings.

title: ICU message format
description: ICU MessageFormat is the standard for complex messages: plurals, selects (gender), and nested combinations in one string — '{n, plural, one {# file} other {# files}}'. Translators reorder freely (word order differs); the format keeps the logic with the message, not in code. Every serious i18n framework speaks ICU.
mechanism: Message strings with {var, plural/select, ...} syntax; runtime formats per locale rules (CLDR data). Translators see the whole sentence with its logic.
algo: O(1) format; CLDR data drives rules.
provenance: Public-harvest: curated from public technical literature, documentation, and established engineering practice.

title: Pluralization
description: Pluralization rules vary wildly: English has 2 forms, Russian 3, Arabic 6, Japanese 1. The code never branches on count — it delegates to the locale's CLDR rules via the message format. Translators provide all forms; the framework picks. Getting this wrong is the most visible i18n bug ('1 files').
mechanism: CLDR plural rules per locale; message format selects the form; translators supply all forms. Code: t('files', {n}) — no branches.
demo:
# CLDR: the RULES differ per locale (code never branches on count)
rules = {
    'en': lambda n: 'one' if n == 1 else 'other',
    'ru': lambda n: 'one' if n % 10 == 1 and n % 100 != 11 else
                    'few' if n % 10 in (2,3,4) and n % 100 not in (12,13,14) else 'many',
    'ja': lambda n: 'other',  # no plurals
    'ar': lambda n: 'zero' if n == 0 else 'one' if n == 1 else 'two' if n == 2 else
                    'few' if 3 <= n % 100 <= 10 else 'many' if 11 <= n % 100 <= 99 else 'other',
}
for lang, rule in rules.items():
    print('%-3s n=2 -> %s' % (lang, rule(2)))
print('translators supply ALL forms; "1 files" is the classic bug')

title: RTL layouts
description: Right-to-left layouts mirror the UI for Arabic, Hebrew, Persian: the whole layout flips (not just text) — navigation moves right, progress fills right-to-left, icons mirror (back arrows point right). CSS logical properties (margin-inline-start, not margin-left) make it automatic. Testing needs real RTL screenshots; LTR assumptions hide everywhere.
mechanism: dir='rtl' + CSS logical properties (inline-start/end, not left/right). Icons: mirror directional ones, not symmetric ones. Test with real RTL content.
demo:
print('RTL: mirror the LAYOUT, not just the text')
print('CSS: margin-inline-start (NOT margin-left)')
print('     padding-inline-end  (NOT padding-right)')
print('     <html dir="rtl"> flips flex/grid automatically')
print('icons: mirror directional (back <-) not symmetric (search)')
print('numbers/dates: still LTR within RTL (bidi algorithm handles)')
print('test with REAL Arabic/Hebrew screenshots: LTR assumptions hide')

title: Locale detection
description: Locale detection picks the initial language: the OS/browser locale list (Accept-Language, in priority order), matched against supported locales with fallback. The user can always override — detection is a default, not a cage. The choice persists; deep links can force a locale (?lang=es). Never geo-locate for language (location != language).
mechanism: Read locale list in priority order; best match against supported (es-MX matches es); user override stored; ?lang= param. Never IP-geolocate for language.

title: Translation workflows
description: Translation workflows move strings from code to translators and back: extract keys (CI), push to the TMS (translation management system), translators work with context (screenshots, descriptions), review, then pull translated files back. Keys carry context (description, screenshot) — translators without context guess. The pipeline runs continuously, not per-release.
mechanism: Extract (CI) -> TMS (translate + review with context) -> pull -> build. Key context mandatory. Continuous, not batched per release.
demo:
print('TRANSLATION PIPELINE (continuous)')
print('1. extract: CI scans code -> keys + context (description, screenshot)')
print('2. push: to TMS (translators see context: no guessing)')
print('3. translate + review (native speakers review)')
print('4. pull: translated files back into the repo')
print('5. build: missing keys fall back (never block the release)')
print('keys WITHOUT context get guessed translations: context is mandatory')

title: Pseudo-localization
description: Pseudo-localization tests i18n without translators: transform the source strings (lengthen 40%, add accents 'Ĥęļļö', wrap with [!! !!]) and run the app. It exposes hardcoded strings (not transformed), layout breaks (long German), and encoding bugs — before real translations arrive. Every string goes through it in CI.
mechanism: Transform en strings: pad + accent + bracket; run the full test suite + screenshots. Failures = i18n bugs. Cheap, automatic, always on.
algo: O(strings) transform; the suite does the rest.

title: Date/number formatting
description: Dates, numbers, and currencies format per locale: 1,234.56 vs 1.234,56 vs ١٬٢٣٤٫٥٦; dates 10/20/2026 vs 20.10.2026. The Intl APIs (Intl.NumberFormat, Intl.DateTimeFormat) handle it — never hand-format. Timezones are explicit; relative time ('2 hours ago') localizes too. Currency needs the code (USD), not just the symbol ($).
mechanism: Intl.* APIs with the locale; never hand-format. Timezone explicit. Currency with code. Relative time via Intl.RelativeTimeFormat.
demo:
print('// Intl.NumberFormat / Intl.DateTimeFormat: never hand-format')
print("new Intl.NumberFormat('de-DE').format(1234.56)  // '1.234,56'")
print("new Intl.NumberFormat('ar-EG').format(1234.56)  // '١٬٢٣٤٫٥٦'")
print("new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US',{dateStyle:'medium'}).format(d)")
print('currency: {style:"currency", currency:"USD"} (code, not just $)')
print('relative: new Intl.RelativeTimeFormat(lang).format(-2, "hour")')
print('timezone EXPLICIT: never the server\'s local')

title: Font support
description: Fonts must cover the scripts you ship: Latin-only fonts tofu CJK/Arabic/Devanagari. The solutions are system font stacks (the OS has the glyphs), webfonts per script (subsetted, lazy-loaded), and font-display: swap (no invisible text). Test every locale's UI in screenshots — tofu boxes are the visible failure.
mechanism: System stack first (native glyphs); webfont subsets per script, lazy; font-display: swap. Screenshot every locale.
demo:
print('FONT STRATEGY PER SCRIPT')
print('system stack: -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Noto Sans", ...')
print('  (the OS HAS the glyphs: cheapest correct)')
print('webfonts: subset per script (latin, cjk, arabic), lazy-load on locale')
print('font-display: swap (never invisible text)')
print('test: screenshot EVERY locale (tofu boxes = visible failure)')

title: i18n QA
description: i18n QA is systematic: pseudo-locale runs, per-locale screenshot diffs, translator review of context, linguistic testing (native speakers clicking through), and functional tests per locale (dates, plurals, RTL). The checklist runs per release for every shipped locale. Bugs found by users in their language erode trust fastest.
mechanism: Pseudo CI -> screenshot diffs per locale -> linguistic pass -> functional per locale. Checklist per release per locale.
demo:
print('I18N QA CHECKLIST (per release, per locale)')
for item in [
    'pseudo-locale: full suite green',
    'screenshot diff vs baseline (layout breaks?)',
    'plurals: 1/2/5 in every plural form',
    'dates/numbers/currency in locale format',
    'RTL: mirrored layout screenshots',
    'fonts: no tofu in any screen',
    'linguistic pass: native speaker clicks through',
]:
    print(' [ ]', item)
print('bugs in the user\'s language erode trust fastest')

title: Translation fallbacks
description: Fallbacks keep the UI working when translations are missing: key -> regional (es-MX -> es) -> base language (es) -> source language (en) -> the key itself (never blank). Missing translations are logged (so they get translated) but never block. The fallback chain is why partial translations ship safely.
mechanism: Chain: exact -> base -> source -> key. Log misses (dashboard of untranslated keys). Never render blank.

title: i18n performance
description: i18n performance is bundle and runtime: locale files split per language (load only the active one), lazy-load on language switch, and ICU data trimmed to shipped locales (full-icu is heavy). Runtime lookups are O(1) hash maps. The English bundle doesn't pay for 40 languages.
mechanism: Per-locale chunks (dynamic import); trim ICU/CLDR data; O(1) lookups. Measure bundle per locale.
demo:
print('I18N PERF')
print('bundle: one chunk per locale (dynamic import); load ONLY the active')
print('ICU data: trim to shipped locales (full-icu is HEAVY)')
print('runtime: O(1) hash lookups (no one notices)')
print('switch: lazy-load the chunk, swap, repaint (<300ms)')
print('the en bundle never pays for 40 languages')

title: Machine translation
description: Machine translation fills the gaps: MT drafts for untranslated keys (marked as machine-translated, reviewed later), MT for user-generated content (reviews, comments — translated on the fly), and MT-assisted human translation (translators post-edit). Quality varies by language pair — high-resource pairs are good, low-resource need human review. Always label MT output.
mechanism: MT API for drafts/UGC; mark machine-translated (review queue); human post-edit for shipped strings. Label everything MT-produced.
demo:
print('MACHINE TRANSLATION ROLES')
print('1. drafts: untranslated keys -> MT now, human review later (MARKED)')
print('2. UGC: reviews/comments translated on the fly (labeled "translated")')
print('3. assist: translators post-edit MT (faster than from scratch)')
print('quality: high-resource pairs good; low-resource = human review')
print('RULE: always label MT output (trust requires honesty)')

title: Glossaries and style
description: Glossaries keep terminology consistent: 'dashboard' is always 'panel' in Spanish, never three different words. The glossary is per product, enforced in the TMS (flags deviations), and owned by the localization team. Style guides cover tone (formal/informal 'you'), and brand terms that never translate. Inconsistency looks unprofessional; glossaries prevent it.
mechanism: Term base in the TMS; deviations flagged; style guide per locale (tone, brand terms). Owned by localization, used by all translators.

title: Testing i18n
description: i18n testing is automated where possible: unit tests for plural/format functions per locale, integration tests rendering key screens per locale, screenshot diffs, and the pseudo-locale suite. The test matrix is locales x critical paths — sampled intelligently (every locale gets smoke, high-traffic locales get full). New strings require tests in at least two locales.
mechanism: Unit (formats/plurals per locale) -> integration (screens per locale) -> visual (diffs) -> pseudo suite. Matrix sampled by traffic.

print('unit: plural/format functions x every locale (fast, always)')
print('integration: critical screens x every locale (render, no crash)')
